<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par107 />Knudtzon (see above, Rem. on {{GHGpar|106|a}}), comparing the Ass.-Bab. usage, would prefer the term ''present'' rather than imperfect, on the ground that the tense expresses what is either actually or mentally present. In any case, the essential difference between the perfect and imperfect consists, he argues, in this, that the perfect simply indicates what is actually complete, while the imperfect places the action, &c., in a more direct relation to the judgement or feeling of the speaker.

More precisely the imperfect serves—

'''1.''' In the sphere of ''past time'':

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|b}}
(''a'') To express actions, &c., which ''continued'' throughout a longer or shorter period,<ref>Cf. the ''Mêšaʿ'' inscription, l. 5, {{GHGheb|text=כי יאנף כמש בארצה|translate=for Chemosh was angry with his land}}. As Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, 3rd ed., § 27, 1 a, remarks, this vivid realization of the accomplishment of the action is especially frequent in poetic and prophetic style.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=6}} ''a mist went up'' continually ({{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲלֶה}}), 2:25, 37:7, 48:10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=8|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, 12, 14, 15, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=15}} f. 20 f., 23 <sup>7</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=2|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=17|hidebook=1}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=4|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=יִמָּלֵא}}), 17:10 f., 51:2 x, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=7}}, 14, 17 ff.38 ff., 24:2, 32:4, 5 ({{GHGheb|text=אוֹדִֽיעֲךָ}}), 47:5, 68:10, 12, 104:6 ff., 106:19, 107:18, 29, 139:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, 15 f., 10:10 f., 15:7 f.—very frequently alternating with a perfect (especially with a frequentative perfect; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=15}}–23 and {{GHGpar|112|e}}), or when the narration is continued by means of an imperfect consecutive.<ref>According to the Masora such imperfects occur in Is 10<sup>13 ''bis''</sup> (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=וְאָסִיר}} might also mean ''I am wont to remove'', &c.), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=57|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=38}}a, also (according to {{GHGpar|49|c}}) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=10}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=10}}. In some other cases {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} is no doubt a dogmatic emendation for {{GHGheb|text=וָ}} (''imperf. consec.'') in order to represent historical statements as promises; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=28|hidebook=1}} [contrasted with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=25|hidebook=1}}], {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=2 bis|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=63|verse=3 ff.|hidebook=1}} and the note on {{GHGpar|53|p}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|c}}
Rem. 1. The imperfect is frequently used in this way after the particles {{GHGheb|text=אָז|translate=then}}, {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם|translate=not yet}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם|translate=before}}, {{GHGheb|text=עַד־|translate=until}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אָז יָשִֽׁיר־משֶׁה|translate=then sang Moses}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=126|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=21}}. (The {{GHGterm|perfect}} is used after {{GHGheb|text=אָז}} when stress is to be laid on the fact that the action has really taken place, and not upon its gradual accomplishment or duration in the past, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=אָז הוּחַל|translate=then began}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=20}}.)<ref>After {{GHGheb|text=אָז|translate=then}} (to announce future events) the imperf. is naturally used in the sense of a future, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=41}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=48}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=51|verse=21}}.</ref> After {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם}} e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם יִשְׁכָּ֫בוּ|translate=before they lay down}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=45|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=3}}, 7, always in the sense of our ''pluperfect''. (In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=15}} instead of the perf. {{GHGheb|text=כִּלָּה}}, the imperf. should be read, as in verse 45; so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=7}} [{{GHGheb|text=יִגָּלֶה}}] an imperf. is co-ordinated with {{GHGheb|text=ידע}}). After {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם}} (sometimes also simply {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=1}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם תֵּצֵא|translate=before thou camest forth}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=33}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=50|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=14}} (perhaps also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=2}} an imperf. was intended instead of {{GHGheb|text=יֻלָּ֫דוּ}}; cf. Wellhausen on {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=2}}; but note also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=25}}, in a similar context, ''before the mountains were settled'', {{GHGheb|text=הָטְכָּ֑עוּ}}, the predicate being separated from {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם}}, by {{GHGheb|text=הָרִים}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=2}}). After {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=17}} (''until I went''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=29|verse=34}}; on the other<section end=par107 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
